<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Wuschelkopf" /></noinclude><section begin="par149" />{{GHGheb|text=חֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ}},<ref>Also combined {{GHGheb|text=חַי־יְהֹוָה וְחֵי נַפְשְׁךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=26|hidebook=1}} ''as the Lord liveth, and as thy soul'' (i.e. ''thou'') ''liveth!'' (Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=11}} read {{GHGheb|text=חַי־יהוה}} instead of the impossible {{GHGheb|text=חַיֶּ֫ךְ}}). On {{GHGheb|text=חַי}} and {{GHGheb|text=חֵי}} in these noun-clauses (prop. ''living is the Lord'', &c.), cf. {{GHGpar|93|aa}}, note.</ref> {{GHGheb|text=חַי אָ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּי נִשְׁבַּ֫עְתִּי}}, &c., as well as after imprecations, see below), and also simple asseverations, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=5}} after {{GHGheb|text=חָלִ֫ילָה לִי|translate=far be it from me}}, but mostly without any introductory formula.

{{GHGmargin-letter|149|b}}
Rem. No certain explanation of these particles has yet been given. According to the usual view, phrases expressing an oath depend on the suppression of an imprecation upon oneself, e.g. ''the Lord do so unto me, if I do it'' equivalent to ''I certainly will not do it''; then naturally {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} properly ''if I do it not'' equivalent to ''I certainly will do it''. It is indeed difficult to understand such self-imprecations, put into the mouth of God, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=34}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=11}}. Possibly, however, the consciousness of the real meaning of the formula was lost at an early period, and {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} simply came to express ''verily'', {{GHGheb|text=אִם|translate=verily not}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=22}}, where, instead of a self-imprecation, a curse is pronounced upon others, read {{GHGheb|text=לְדָוִד}} with the LXX for {{GHGheb|text=לְאֹֽיְבֵי דָוִד}}.

Examples:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|149|c}}
(''a'') The particles {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} and {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} used after the utterance of an oath and after formulae of swearing, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=11}} (see note on ''a'') {{GHGheb|text=חַי־יְהֹוָה וְחֵי נַפְשֶׁ֫ךָ אִם־אִֽעֱשֶׂה אֶת־הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה|translate=as the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=45}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=16}} (after {{GHGheb|text=חַי יְהֹוָה}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=39}} and 29:6 {{GHGheb|text=חַי־י׳}} is followed by a simple {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (after {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁבַּ֫עְתִּי|translate=I adjure you}}); cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=29|hidebook=1}}; spoken by God, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=34}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=11}}; similarly {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=37}} f.; spoken by God, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=24}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} occurs first with the perfect in the sense of a prophetic perfect, {{GHGpar|106|n}}, but in the parallel clause with the imperfect; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=6}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=52}} the negative oath introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אִם־אָ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִם־אַתָּה}} is immediately afterwards continued by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the imperfect.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=10}} the threat introduced in verse 8 by {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} is, after a long parenthesis, resumed with {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנִי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|149|d}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} and {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} after formulae of cursing, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=כֹּה יַֽעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ אֱלֹהִים וְכֹה יוֹסִיף אִם־תְּכַחֵד מִמֶּ֫נִּי דָבָר וג׳|translate=God do so to thee, and more also! thou shalt not hide anything from me}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=22}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} follows the curse, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=44}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=23}} (here with a perfect), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=35}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=34}} the preceding {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} is repeated before {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=13}} the purport of the asseveration is repeated (after the insertion of a conditional sentence) in the perfect consecutive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|149|e}}
(''c'') {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} and {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} as simple particles of asseveration, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=מָגֵן אִם־יֵרָאֶה וָרֹמַח וג׳|translate=truly, there was not a shield and spear seen}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=28}} (in the middle of the sentence); after {{GHGheb|text=חָלִ֫ילָה חָלִ֫ילָה|translate=absit}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}} with the imperf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=9}}, with the perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=20}}.<section end="par149" /><noinclude>
